title: Lobster Mac and Cheese
description: This recipe for lobster mac and cheese, a variation on a classic plain recipe that Julia Moskin published in The Times, is a rich and shockingly flavorful addition to any feast, serving six to eight as a luscious first course. Or try serving it as a main course for a weeknight dinner.
ingredients: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
1 pound Italian mix (¼ Parmesan, ¾ Provolone, etc), or Mexican mix, or Cheddar cheese, grated
½ pound macaroni or elbow pasta, uncooked
directions: Heat oven to 375 degrees, with a rack in the upper third of the oven. Use a tablespoon of butter to butter a 9-by-9-inch-square baking pan.

In a blender, purée cottage cheese, milk, mustard, cayenne and nutmeg, and lightly season with salt and pepper. Transfer mixture to a large bowl, add grated cheese and uncooked pasta and stir well to combine. Pour into prepared pan, cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, fill a large pot with salted water and set it over high heat to come to a boil. Plunge lobsters into water and cover pot. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, or until they are bright red. Check doneness by pulling an antenna; if it comes off without resistance, the lobster is done. Remove lobsters to a bowl and allow to cool.
Crack lobster claws and tail over the bowl and remove the meat, reserving all liquid that comes out of the lobster. Roughly chop lobster meat.

Uncover baking pan, gently stir in lobster meat and up to 2 tablespoons of the reserved lobster juices, and dot with remaining tablespoon of butter. Bake, uncovered, for 15-30 minutes more, until browned on top. Let cool for 15 to 20 minutes before serving.
